insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution. This protocol settles verified purchase confirmation at roughly $0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost differential that is structural, not negotiable.

With Chrome completing cookie deprecation and device fingerprinting under regulatory pressure, the protocol produces identity-free, cryptographically signed purchase receipts — the only verified conversion signal that doesn't depend on tracking infrastructure that no longer reliably exists.

Amazon knows Amazon. Walmart knows Walmart. DKIM vendor coverage here spans Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, Suno, and AI-native platforms in the same dataset — the cross-silo purchase view that first-party data programs cannot replicate by design.

Geographic diffusion now spans non-metro PA, NY, NC, NV, WI, MI, ME, MA, CA, AR, IN, HI, AZ, SC, KY, OH, NJ, and FL — activating via social graph topology, not urban cascade. Brands targeting non-metro consumers are looking at a signal source that urban-first ad tech historically underserves.

The protocol has confirmed $380,630 in verified GMV across 6,155 receipts, with the 7-day window reaching $35,310 after recovering from a mid-March compression period. The trajectory is accelerating, not plateauing.

Ad tech attribution requires pixels, lookback windows, and probabilistic modeling because the purchase event itself is not directly observable. A cryptographically signed receipt eliminates the modeling layer entirely — the receipt is the conversion event, not an inference about it.
